items.title: Cool adaptations: How fish survive in the Antarctic Ocean

items.title: Crystal boundaries help hydrogen sensors work in hot, humid air
items.summary: Hydrogen could play an important role in cleaner energy systems, but even small leaks can create safety risks. Reliable sensors are therefore essential wherever hydrogen is produced, stored, transported or used. A persistent problem is humidity: water molecules can cover the active surfaces of hydrogen detectors and prevent them from responding accurately, particularly in hot, moisture-rich environments.
items.imageAlt: Crystal boundaries help hydrogen sensors work in hot, humid air

items.title: Researcher uses AI to predict probabilities for chemical processes
items.summary: Quantum chemistry can be used to calculate the probabilities of which chemical processes will occur. This involves a great deal of programming work. Dr. Michael F. Peintinger from the Mulliken Center for Theoretical Chemistry at the University of Bonn has investigated what happens when artificial intelligence is used for this purpose. His work is published in the Journal of Computational Chemistry.
